data.name: Dhuha
data.gender_notes: Dhuha is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dhuha refers to the period of dawn, symbolizing renewal and a fresh start. The name Dhuha carries the meaning “Early morning” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Dhuha usually hope their child will grow to embody early morning and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Dhuha is also the name of the second of the five daily prayers.
data.etymology: Dhuha belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Early morning.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dhuha total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: ضحى
in_arabic.meaning: اسم يدل على ضوء النهار واشراقه
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مشتق من الضحى، وهو الوقت الذي تظهر فيه الشمس وتشع نورها، ويعبر عن النور والاشراق، وقد ورد ذكره في القرآن الكريم في سورة الضحى، ويعتبر من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني روحانية ودلالات إيجابية في الثقافة الإسلامية

in_urdu.name: ضحی
in_urdu.meaning: دین کے روشنی اور صبح کی شعاع
in_urdu.long_meaning: یہ نام عربی زبان کے 'ضحى' سے ماخوذ ہے، جو صبح کی روشنی اور شمس کے اشراق کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، قرآن مجید میں سورہ الضحیٰ کے طور پر اس کا ذکر کیا گیا ہے، اور اسلامی ثقافت میں اسے ایک ایسے نام کے طور پر سمجھا جاتا ہے جو روحانی معنی اور مثبت اشارات رکھتا ہے، خاص طور پر جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی معاشرے میں

in_hindi.name: दुहा

in_english.name: Dhuha
in_english.long_meaning: The name Dhuha originates from the Arabic root 'ḍ-h-w', which means 'morning light' or 'dawn', it is mentioned in the Quran as Surah Ad-Dhuha, symbolizing hope, guidance, and illumination, in Islamic tradition, it signifies a child born during the morning hours or one who brings light and positivity into the world

data.cultural_impact: Dhuha is an Arabic term that means "the dawn" in English. In Islamic culture, it refers to the time between the last hour of the night (adhan for Fajr) and the appearance of the sun (Fajr prayer), lasting approximately 15-20 minutes. During this time, Muslims put extra effort into their prayers and acts of worship, seeking the blessings of the early morning hours.
data.spiritual_significance: Dhuha is a profoundly spiritual time for Muslims as it represents the beginning of a new day from a divine perspective. The Prophet Mohammad (peace be upon him) emphasized the importance of making Dhuha, as it offers greater reward for only a few additional voluntary prayers. In Sufi circles, it is believed to be a sacred time for personal reflection, contemplation, and increased closeness to Allah. This is an opportunity for Muslims to purify their intentions, seek Allah's forgiveness, and renew their commitment to living an Islamic life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Early morning" symbolizes Dhuha refers to the period of dawn, symbolizing renewal and a fresh start.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Dhuha serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of early morning.
